newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta index ends up, focus on Pikko.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta index ends up, focus on Pikko.

text.p: Jakarta stocks edged higher at the close on Tuesday, with the focus on Bank Pikko before it was suspended in late trading, brokers said.
The Jakarta composite index rose 1.58 points, or 0.25 percent, to close at 638.22 points.
Advancers led decliners by 53 to 47 with 84 issues unchanged.
Total turn-over was 354.20 billion rupiah against 302 billion rupiah on Monday.
"This suspension of Bank Pikko is the first suspension this year. I think the stock exchange authority has taken the right decision as the rise was just too spectacular," one broker said.
Bank Pikko rose 2,700 rupiah, or 207.69 percent, to 4,000 rupiah with 21.7 million shares traded on take-over rumours before it was suspended, brokers said.
"The bank told us on Monday that the firm had no new corporate actions that had not been published," the exchange's head of the monitoring division, Hamud Balfast, told Reuters.
"But then this morning we read a story in the Neraca daily that an investor wanted to buy a large stake in the bank," Balfast said.
Balfast said the exchange expected to get details from the bank as soon as possible and that trading of the stock was likely to resume on Thursday depending on the response from the bank.
The Jakarta stock exchange will be closed on Wednesday due to a public holiday.

Snack food firm Mayora ended unchanged at 875 rupiah, after touching a year-low of 825 rupiah in moderate volume, after reports that the country's 1997 coffee production was expected to be below earlier forecasts.

Indonesia's 1997 coffee production was expected to be some 30 percent short of an originally forecast 480,000 tonnes due to bad weather, the chairman of the Association of Indonesian Coffee Exporters (AICE), Oesman Soedargo, said on Monday.
Cigarette maker Sampoerna was unchanged at 10,300 rupiah following a rise in the price of the firm's main Dji Sam Soe brand to 1,800 rupiah from 1,700 rupiah effective from Monday.
Retailer Matahari was traded at the cross board at 3,300 rupiah, down from the previous 3,325 rupiah, with some 10 million shares traded, but the parties involved were not clear, brokers said.
